transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-15 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~52 minutes | Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Carlos (Medigram), Priya (Medigram), Laura (Medigram security), Ben (SRE)

Summary: quick recap at top, see action items for owners. A few sections auto-gen might be off.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Samira): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, hope you're all well. Quick agenda — catalog gaps, pinned versions, canary plan and any security open items.
00:18 Speaker 2 (Carlos): yep thanks, Samira. We hit a couple of weirdnesses in the last run where the LLM drifted on diagnosis summaries when sequence length got bigger. We're anxious about swapovers — need a safety net.
00:32 Speaker 1 (Samira): Got it, that's what we're here for. Ethan, quick status on the benchmark runs you started?
00:40 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Yeah, we did a shallow run yesterday — small sample — and we saw the higher-temp variant had 12% more tail latency under burst. But that's on hosted instance, not our dedicated replica. There's some noise, transcription may say had not, I mean it wasn't stable yet.
01:02 Speaker 2 (Carlos): when you say "hosted instance" do you mean Redwood Hosted or your dedicated pilot infra?
01:06 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Redwood hosted. We'll re-run on the dedicated commit to match your env. We need your traffic sample to make it realistic.
01:12 Speaker 4 (Priya): we'll get that to you. Also want to confirm: how do you handle KV cache across model variants? If we pin to model A and fallback to B, does state carry over?
01:25 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Good question — KV cache persists per model family in our setup; if the variants are compatible (same architecture and kv-layout) we can reuse the cache, but if quantization or param layout differs you'll need warm-start or accept a cold start. There's a small chance of mismatch causing hallucination if tokens align differently — we should enumerate compatible pairs.
01:50 Speaker 1 (Samira): which is why we suggested a pinned primary and two fallback tiers: same-arch quantized low-cost, and cross-arch safe degrade. We'll add compatibility notes in the catalog sheet.
02:05 Speaker 5 (Laura): from security, we need an explicit KMS flow and audit log example. Also retention: can't keep raw PII beyond 30 days for this pilot — make sure redwood retention settings are clear.
02:18 Speaker 1 (Samira): absolutely, Laura. I'll send the SOC2 + KMS diagram. For retention, we can set the tenant retention policy for pilot to 30 days and show audit logs.
02:30 Speaker 2 (Carlos): on rollback playbook — what's the fastest escape hatch?
02:36 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Fastest is route-level rollback: route requests to previous pinned revision with a hard pin timeout; alternative is gradual traffic shift with 10% steps and health checks on latency, error-rate and quality (we use prompt-level evals). If the new model degrades quality, we auto-fallback to the previous pinned variant. There's also a region fallback if you need to prefer latency.
03:05 Speaker 6 (Ben): do health checks include token-level cost impact? we worry about sudden cost jumps on high-volume.
03:13 Speaker 3 (Ethan): yes, cost is included in the SLOs — token per call and average token length capture that. We'll add cost delta alerts to the canary gating.
03:30 Speaker 2 (Carlos): can you show the catalog comparison now?
03:35 Speaker 1 (Samira): we'll screen-share the spreadsheet — link posted in chat (https://redwood.example.com/sheets/pilot-catalog-compare) but I'll summarise: Candidate A (rwd-8b-v2) — strong short-form, cheaper after int8 quant; Candidate B (open-13-compat) — better long-tail but 20% higher latency; Candidate C (fallback-small) — ultra-low cost, lower quality but fast. We've flagged compatibility and whether kv-cache is shareable.
04:12 Speaker 3 (Ethan): important note: open-13-compat uses a different kv-layout so fallback from rwd-8b will cause cold cache. For user flows that need sustained context we recommend same-arch fallback first.
04:32 Speaker 2 (Carlos): ok that explains the drift. For the diagnostic summaries we likely need the long-tail behavior of B, but we want to keep cost in check. Suggest pinned primary as rwd-8b for day-to-day and shadow B for the longest cases then promote if shadow quality beats baseline.
04:56 Speaker 1 (Samira): that's a good compromise — shadowing + promote rule. We'll add an eval harness: shadow responses compared by our evals sheet.
05:10 Speaker 5 (Laura): security question: If we shadow, does user data leave your enclave? We can't forward PII to unapproved models.
05:20 Speaker 3 (Ethan): shadowing can be done in two ways — internal shadowing (within your private deployment) or cross-model shadow where we route copy to hosted catalog; for your case we'd keep shadowing internal inside your private VPC so PII doesn't leave. Requires Private deployment or VPC connector.
05:40 Speaker 4 (Priya): we are evaluating private; timeline for on-prem package?
05:45 Speaker 1 (Samira): on-prem is possible but usually takes 4–6 weeks to provision with our engineering onboarding; VPC connector can be faster — 1–2 weeks depending on approvals. We'll map both options.
06:05 Speaker 2 (Carlos): timeline — we need canary in prod week of 7/28. Is that realistic?
06:12 Speaker 3 (Ethan): yes if we get traffic sample and Ethan runs benchmarks by 7/18 and we confirm pinned candidates by 7/16 we can schedule a controlled canary for 7/28.
06:28 Speaker 1 (Samira): ok let's lock milestones: Samira to update sheet 7/16; Carlos to send sample 7/17; Ethan to run large-scale bench 7/18. Laura to confirm KMS by 7/20.
06:45 Speaker 2 (Carlos): also, can we have an escape route to route back to OpenAI if your cluster saturates? Competitor fallback?
06:53 Speaker 3 (Ethan): we can add a cross-provider fallback policy but that adds complexity — token accounting and PII controls differ. We'll document the tradeoffs.
07:04 Speaker 5 (Laura): note — any cross-provider fallback needs outbound egress review from legal.
07:10 Speaker 1 (Samira): noted. We'll include that in the security checklist.
07:18 Speaker 2 (Carlos): about version pinning mechanics: can we pin at route level per customer cohort?
07:24 Speaker 3 (Ethan): yes—per-route and per-tenant pins supported. You can set a hierarchy: tenant pin > route pin > global default. And pin expiry so it auto-falls back after a TTL if not unpinned.
07:42 Speaker 4 (Priya): TTL is useful. For rollbacks, will there be a controlled freeze so no mid-flight swaps?
07:49 Speaker 3 (Ethan): we support freeze points: freeze means new model deployments are blocked for selected routes and autoscale continues, also an option to drain sessions for safe switch.
08:05 Speaker 1 (Samira): sounds like we have a clear plan. Any other open items?
08:10 Speaker 6 (Ben): quick ops note — please share the exact Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboard names so we can hook alerts.
08:18 Speaker 3 (Ethan): will share prometheus targets and the dashboard JSON.
08:22 Speaker 2 (Carlos): last thing: does Redwood have pre-defined quantization recommendations? Our infra team worried about int8 vs int4 quality tradeoffs.
08:31 Speaker 1 (Samira): we do — in Optimize we recommend quant profile per workload. For diagnosis summaries int8 tends to preserve quality; int4 may drop the rare-case reasoning. We'll recommend quant profiles in the sheet.
08:48 Speaker 5 (Laura): can you put that in writing for compliance folks?
08:52 Speaker 1 (Samira): yes — will include in the catalog notes.
09:00 Speaker 2 (Carlos): ok thanks — we'll reconvene next week same time.
09:05 Speaker 1 (Samira): thanks all, meeting adjourned.
